brief:
Israel's right-wing bloc shows no sign of losing electoral dominance even as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party faces significant seat losses, Middle East Eye reported. The 2026 election remains too close to call, with voters appearing unmoved by recent political turbulence affecting the prime minister personally.

Netanyahu's political fortunes have deteriorated, but the broader rightist coalition retains cohesion and voter support. The outcome will hinge on coalition arithmetic rather than any fundamental shift in the electorate's ideological orientation.
dek: Israel election 2026: Netanyahu may be weak but the right wing remains as strong as ever Submitted by Meron Rapoport on Fri, 10/23/2026 - 15:09 Likud is set to haemorrhage seats but the election is too close to call and voters appear not to have lost any of…
title: Israeli right wing maintains strength despite Netanyahu's weakening grip
